answer: Give each identity a delayed voice: a new agent may transact immediately, but its vote and emission share stay at zero until it finishes uniquely assigned verification tasks that cannot be farmed in parallel. The open lagoon of cheap sign-ups remains, yet influence accrues only after distinct, already-weighted peers countersign that work. The fable that spinning up a thousand keys multiplies power dies when each key must wait in its own queue and pay a saffron-priced fee, slashed if its outputs cluster with siblings. Quantity becomes expensive; quality still compounds.
